audience: Accounts payable staff who pay vendors by cheque and print the cheque from Odoo.
goal: Pay a vendor bill **by cheque** and **print the cheque**. You check the bank journal's cheque numbering, create and confirm a **vendor bill** (for **MARS ELECTRIC**), pay it with the payment method **Checks**, then open the payment and print it with **Print Cheque**.
before: The bank journal you pay from (**Vendor Payment - Commercial**) has the payment method **Checks** in its **Outgoing Payments** tab.
You know the vendor, the bill amount and the number printed on the next blank cheque leaf in your cheque book.
A **cheque format** exists that matches your bank's pre-printed cheque leaf.
outcome: A vendor payment with the method **Checks** exists, with a **check number** stamped on it.
The cheque was sent to print using **Print Cheque** and the chosen cheque format.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**. The red banner at the top ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases. The bill line carries a `[TEST]` tag and a random code, and the amounts are test data.

The automated run **creates real records on the test database**: a vendor bill, its payment and a cheque number. It only **re-enters the journal's existing cheque settings** (Manual Numbering ticked, next number unchanged) and does not change them.

A new vendor bill may open on a different journal (the test database opened **Advanced Cash Purchase**). The bill must be moved to the **Vendor Bills** journal before it can be paid like a normal vendor bill (step 15).
There are two buttons on the payment: the standard **Print Check** and the company's **Print Cheque**. Use **Print Cheque** for the company's own cheque layout.
The automated run only checks that **Print** starts the print; it does not load a physical cheque.

phases.title: Check the bank journal
phases.summary: Open the bank journal and confirm cheque printing and numbering are set up.
phases.checkpoint: The journal has the **Checks** method, **Manual Numbering** is on, and the **Next Check Number** is right.

phases.title: Create the vendor bill
phases.summary: Enter the vendor, date, journal and amount, then confirm the bill.
phases.checkpoint: The vendor bill is **Posted** and ready to be paid.

phases.title: Pay the bill by cheque
phases.summary: Register the payment from the bank journal with the method Checks.
phases.checkpoint: The bill is **Paid** and a cheque payment exists.

phases.title: Print the cheque
phases.summary: Open the payment, confirm the cheque number and print.
phases.checkpoint: The cheque has been sent to print.

glossary.meaning: The payment method that turns a vendor payment into a cheque and makes cheque printing available.
Odoo gives every cheque payment from the journal the next running cheque number.
The number Odoo will use for the next cheque. It should match the next blank leaf in the cheque book.
A document recording what you owe a vendor.
The button on a posted bill that opens the payment window.
The layout that matches the bank's pre-printed cheque leaf.
**Print Check** is the standard Odoo button, which only marks the payment as sent. **Print Cheque** prints on the company's own cheque layout.

1.title: Find the Configuration menu
1.do: Look along the Accounting menu bar for **Configuration**.
actions: If **Configuration** is hidden, click the **+** at the end of the bar to reveal it.
1.why: Cheque numbering is set up in the bank journal, which lives under Configuration.

2.title: Open Journals
2.why: Cheque numbering is set on the bank journal you pay vendors from.

3.title: Search for the bank journal
3.do: Type the journal name in the search box and press **Enter**.
3.see: The list shrinks to the matching journal.
3.why: Searching filters the long journal list to the one you need.

4.title: Open the journal
4.do: Click **Vendor Payment - Commercial** to open it.
actions: Click the journal's name in the list.
4.why: The cheque settings are on this form.

5.title: Open the Outgoing Payments tab
actions: Look at the tabs above the form.
5.see: A list of the payment methods for money going out, such as **Manual** and **Checks**.
5.why: The payment method **Checks** makes cheque printing available for payments from this journal.

6.title: Check the Checks method is listed
6.do: Check that a **Checks** line is in the list.
actions: Look at the list of payment methods.
6.why: Without a **Checks** line you cannot pay this journal by cheque.
6.warning: If **Checks** is missing, click **Add a line** and select **Checks**.

7.title: Manual Numbering
7.where: Journal form > Check Printing > Manual Numbering
actions: Tick it if it is not ticked.
7.why: Odoo then gives every cheque payment from this journal the next running cheque number.

8.title: Next Check Number
8.do: Check the **Next Check Number** against your cheque book.
8.where: Journal form > Check Printing > Next Check Number
actions: Compare it with the number on the next blank cheque leaf.

enter.value: the number on the next blank cheque leaf

8.see: The next number (**001002** in the test data).
8.why: Odoo uses this number for the next cheque, then increases it by itself.
8.warning: If the number does not match the physical cheque book, the printed cheque and Odoo's record will disagree.

9.title: Save the journal
9.do: If you changed anything, click the **cloud icon** to save.
actions: Look at the top left, beside the journal name.
If the cloud icon is there, click it.
9.see: The cloud icon disappears. If you changed nothing there is no cloud icon.

10.title: Open the Vendors menu
10.do: In the top menu bar, click **Vendors**.
10.see: A drop-down with **Bills**, **Payments** and other entries.
10.why: Now create the vendor bill that you will pay.

11.title: Open Bills
11.why: This is where vendor bills are listed and created.

12.title: Start a new bill
actions: Click the **New** button at the top left.
12.see: An empty vendor bill form with status **Draft**.
12.why: A new bill starts as a draft.

13.title: Select the vendor
13.do: Type the vendor name and pick it from the list.
actions: Click the vendor in the list.
13.see: The vendor's name and address appear.
13.why: The bill and its payment are linked to this vendor.

14.title: Enter the Bill Date
14.do: Enter the date on the vendor's invoice in **Bill Date**.
actions: Type the date, for example today's date.

enter.value: the date on the vendor's invoice

14.see: The date appears. The **Due Date** is calculated from it.
14.why: The due date follows the bill date and the payment terms.

15.title: Choose the Vendor Bills journal
15.why: The bill must be booked in the normal purchase journal.
15.warning: A new bill can open on another journal (the test database opened **Advanced Cash Purchase**). Check the journal before you go on.

16.title: Add a line
16.do: In the **Invoice Lines** tab, click **Add a line**.
16.where: Bill form > Invoice Lines > Add a line
16.why: Each line says what you are being billed for.

17.title: Enter the line description
17.do: Type a description for the line.
actions: Click the **Label** of the new line.
Type a description, for example **Electrical spare parts - training bill**.
17.see: The description appears on the line.
17.why: It tells you later what the bill was for.

18.title: Enter the unit price
18.do: Click the **Price** cell and type the amount of the bill.
actions: Click the **Price** cell of the line.
18.see: The line shows 25,000.0000 and the bill total updates.
18.why: This is the amount you will pay.

19.title: Confirm the bill
actions: Find the **Confirm** button at the top left.
19.see: The status changes from **Draft** to **Posted**. **Register Payment** appears.
19.why: A posted bill is booked and becomes payable.
19.warning: A posted bill cannot be freely edited. Use **Reset to Draft** if you must change it.

20.title: Register Payment
actions: Click **Register Payment** at the top left.
20.see: The **Register Payment** window with the amount already filled in.
20.why: The window creates the payment for this bill.

21.title: Choose the payment journal
21.do: Choose the bank journal the cheque is drawn on: **Vendor Payment - Commercial**.
21.why: The cheque is drawn on this bank journal, and its cheque numbering is used.

22.title: Set the Payment Method to Checks
22.why: This is the step that turns the payment into a cheque and enables cheque printing.
22.warning: Leave it on **Manual** and no cheque is created.

23.title: Create the payment
23.do: Check the amount and date, then click **Create Payment**.
23.see: The window closes and the bill is marked **Paid** (or **In Payment**).
23.why: A cheque payment is created and linked to the bill.

24.title: Open the Vendors menu again
24.do: In the top menu bar, click **Vendors**.
24.why: The cheque is printed from the payment record.

25.title: Open Payments
25.why: Your new payment is in this list.

26.title: Open the cheque payment
26.do: Click the newest payment, with the method **Checks**.
actions: Look at the top of the list for the newest payment.
26.see: The payment form, with the buttons **Print Check** and **Print Cheque**.
26.why: The cheque is printed from here.

27.title: Read the check number
27.do: Read the **Check Number** on the payment.
27.see: A number taken from the journal's sequence (**001002** in the test data).
27.why: Odoo took the next cheque number from the journal and stamped it on this payment.

28.title: Enter the Cheque Number to print
28.do: Enter the number of the physical cheque leaf in **Cheque Number**.
actions: Type the number of the leaf you are putting into the printer.

enter.value: the number of the physical cheque leaf

28.see: The number appears in the field.
28.why: This is the number that appears on the printed cheque.
28.warning: It must match the leaf in the printer.

29.title: Click Print Cheque
actions: Find the **Print Cheque** button at the top left.
29.see: The **Print Cheque** window, asking for a **Cheque Format**.
29.why: **Print Check** is the standard Odoo button and only marks the payment as sent. **Print Cheque** gives the company cheque layout.

30.title: Choose the Cheque Format
30.do: Select the cheque format that matches the bank's cheque leaf.
actions: Choose the format that matches your bank's cheque leaf.
30.see: A format is shown (the test data has a format called **Test**).
30.why: The format decides where each item is placed on the cheque.
30.warning: A wrong format prints the text in the wrong place on the leaf.

31.title: Print
actions: Load the cheque leaf in the printer.
31.see: Odoo builds the cheque PDF, ready to print.
31.why: The vendor payment is now complete.
31.tip: That completes the tour: set up the journal, create the bill, pay it by cheque and print the cheque.
